proposal.title: Plugin configuration of routes in the recipe
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: The code of an application sets the plugin options of each route in @route(...): the auth rule, the channel channels, the openapi options, the env requirements. Every installation of that application gets the same values.

An installation cannot change them. The plugins section of the recipe switches plugins on for all the applications together and does not address a route. Changing an option at runtime would need a management application that does not exist.
Each installation must be able to decide the rules of its routes in its recipe, without a management application.

section.title: kajenn today
section.fact: RoutedApplication.__init__ plugs auth, channel, pydantic and openapi on the application router. The only option it sets is channels at router level. Nothing is read from the recipe.

The plugins section of the recipe has plugin children. Each one switches a plugin on and carries the options handed to router.plug(code, **options). The section belongs to the server and applies to every routed application.
The plugins of the plugins section are plugged by server.arm_router on the first access to route made once a server owns the application.
ApplicationGrammar is the grammar every application inherits. Its elements are parameters, request and databases.
An application reads its own part of the recipe at applications.<code>.<path>.
The recipe can declare an application element with code _server. It customises the management application and its class must be ServerApplication or a subclass.
ServerApplication is a RoutedApplication with code _server. Its sections (users, tokens, tasks, monitor, databases, k8s, applications) are attached with add_branches.
The auth section of _server is attached inside the constructor, when the first login method is registered.
The lifespan startup runs on_startup of the applications in registration order. The activation of an application is on_startup, then ready.
In the main process only _server answers at once; every other application waits for its ready. In the dedicated process of an application the applications answer at once.
An application declared with spawner is a RemoteApplication in the main process. The real application class is built in the spawned process, from the same recipe.
An application added to a running server is built from its application node, registered and then activated.

The configuration of a running server is a genro-bag tree. The server subscribes to its applications branch with subscribe(id, insert=..., delete=...): a node written there adds an application, a node taken away removes it. genro-bag subscribe also takes update and any callbacks.
A spawned process loads its configuration from a file or a template when it starts. In kbus_mixin.py, spawner.py and remote_application.py no code sends it a later change of the configuration.
register_application is a sync method.
discover returns the nodes() tree filtered by the channel of the request and by the tags of the caller: an entry the caller may not execute is not listed.
The OpenAPI document derives security of an operation from the auth rule in force on the entry.

A value written without a name in a recipe element becomes the value of its node; the keywords become its attributes. shop.parameters("x", currency="EUR") gives a node with value "x" and attribute currency. A node that receives children loses that value: after cfg.plugins("x").plugin(code="logging") the value of the plugins node is its children and "x" is gone. plugins.plugin("logging") raises ValueError: the collection key needs the attribute code.

section.title: genro-routes 0.30.1
section.fact: routing.configure(target, **options) acts on the router of one routing class. target is "<plugin>" for the router level or "<plugin>/<selector>" for its entries. It is also a dict with the key target, or a list of such dicts. options are the parameters of the configure method of that plugin.
The selector is a glob matched against the entry names of that router, several separated by commas. It does not descend into the sections. A selector that matches no entry raises KeyError.
A plugin that is not on the router raises AttributeError. An option the plugin does not know raises a pydantic ValidationError.
routing.configure("auth/<name>", rule="") opens an entry whose code declares an auth_rule. A non-empty rule replaces the one of the code.
A value written at router level (routing.configure("auth", rule=...)) applies to the entries that declare none. An entry that declares its own value in the code keeps it.

routing.configure("?") returns the description of the router: for each plugin the router-level config and the value in force on each entry (overrides), then the sections under routers. It reports the values in force and does not say where a value comes from. Its shape is not the shape routing.configure takes as input.

Parameters of configure: auth takes rule, channel takes channels, env takes requires, pydantic takes disabled. The kajenn openapi plugin takes method, tags, summary, description, deprecated, security_scheme, security.

When the routes are resolved before a plugin class is registered, the options written in @route(...) for that plugin are lost. A routing.configure call made after the plugin is plugged writes the option and the plugin applies it.

section.title: applications_broadcast
section.fact: On origin/develop f9487ec (PR 147, issue 142) applications_broadcast(method_name, *args, on_error=None, reverse=False, **kwargs) is an async method of the server. It calls the @broadcast_hook of that name on every application, in registration order, and returns [(code, result)]. An application whose class has no such hook is skipped. An application that raises goes to on_error(code, exception); with on_error=None the first exception reaches the caller.

On origin/develop f9487ec a method is a broadcast hook when any definition of its name along the MRO carries @broadcast_hook. A route whose method has the name of a broadcast hook raises ValueError when the application is registered (routed_application.py:239).

On origin/develop f9487ec the RemoteApplication of an application declared with spawner forwards every @broadcast_hook of the real class to the spawned process with remote_call, a kbus call with a timeout. The names RemoteApplication defines itself stay local: on_startup waits for joined, on_shutdown does nothing, because the spawned process runs both in its own lifespan.

list.item: The recipe of an installation names a route of an application and writes the options of one plugin for it.
The value of the recipe replaces the value written in @route(...) for that route. The two are not combined.
A route the recipe does not name keeps the value of the code.
The recipe can close a route the code leaves open and open a route the code closes.
Two installations of the same code have different rules.
No management application is needed: the recipe is enough.
A route named in the recipe that does not exist gives at most a warning. The boot goes on.
The plugin configuration can change on a running server, like other parts of the configuration. A subscription updates the plugins when it changes.

section.title: Recipe
section.p: The example application Shop attaches a section products with three routes. In the code list has no rule; insert and delete have auth_rule="shop_admin". Their URLs are /shop/products/list, /shop/products/insert, /shop/products/delete.
section.code:
shop = cfg.applications().application(code="shop", app_class=Shop)
shop_plugin_auth = shop.plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") shop_plugin_auth.configure(route="products/list,products/insert", rule="staff") shop_plugin_auth.configure(route="products/delete", rule="boss")
shop_plugin_channel = shop.plugin_configuration(plugin="channel") shop_plugin_channel.configure(route="products/list", channels="api,mcp")

list.item: plugin_configuration is an element of ApplicationGrammar: every application has it, _server included. It is written only under an application element.
One plugin_configuration block names one plugin. The plugins are configured separately.

Each configure line carries route and the parameters of the configure method of that plugin. route is the path of one route, or the paths of several routes separated by commas. Each path is complete, relative to the application, written as in the URL after the mount, without a leading slash.
Every plugin present on the router of the application can be configured, a plugin registered from outside included.
_server is configured by declaring application(code="_server", app_class=ServerApplication) in the recipe and writing plugin_configuration under it.

section.title: What kajenn calls
section.p: kajenn adds no syntax of its own for the options: each configure line becomes one call of routing.configure of genro-routes on the routing class that owns the route.

list.item: The plugin of the block gives the first part of the target. The path gives the routing class and the name of the entry.

After these calls /shop/products/list asks for the tag staff and answers on the channel mcp too; /shop/products/delete asks for boss instead of shop_admin; /shop/products/insert asks for staff instead of shop_admin.
A KeyError of routing.configure (no entry with that name) becomes the warning.
A route of a section attached after the hook ran does not exist when the hook runs: its line is a line that names a route that does not exist.
A line that names a plugin that is not on the router, or an option the plugin does not know, is not applied either. Nothing stops.

rule.why: Defensive code prevents only the stupid errors; the dangerous ones pass anyway. An error has consequences for who made it.

section.rule: kajenn adds no defensive code against errors in the plugin configuration: no boot stop, no restore of earlier values, no handling of a hook that refuses.

section.title: The plugin_configuration hook

list.item: Every application has a hook plugin_configuration, marked @broadcast_hook (kajenn-org/kajenn#142).
The server calls it on every application with applications_broadcast("plugin_configuration").
The default does nothing. RoutedApplication reads its plugin_configuration blocks from the recipe and makes the calls above. An application with no block in the recipe does nothing.
A subclass redefines the hook to refuse a configuration or to take the export of its router before the configuration is applied.
No hook runs after the configuration is applied.
For an application declared with spawner the hook runs in the spawned process, where the application is built. Who calls it there at boot is open (d-spawned-boot).
The server calls the hook in the lifespan startup, before on_startup: no request arrives before the configuration.
After the boot the plugin_configuration blocks of an application can change in the configuration of the running server.
A change on a running server is a new configuration. There are no actions that insert or delete a single line: the new configuration only says which values there are.
A subscription updates the plugins of that application with the values of the new configuration.
To give a route its code value back, the new configuration writes that value.

An application declared with spawner needs nothing specific to plugins. Any change of the configuration, of plugins or of anything else, is carried to the spawned process, which applies it to its own configuration. Its own subscriptions fire there, the one of plugin_configuration included.

The hook runs before any configuration that does not come from the code: the subscription goes through the hook of that application, so the application can refuse a change made on a running server too.
kajenn adds no log line, no route and no discovery field for this.
nodes() called with the tags of a user says which routes that user may execute. discover already does it.
routing.configure("?") gives the values in force.

Who wants the differences takes the export in the hook, before the configuration is applied, and keeps it. A method compares that export with the export taken when it is called. After the configuration is applied the router no longer holds the values of the code: the first export cannot be rebuilt later from the running server.

section.title: JSON form
section.p: A JSON form of the plugin configuration, such as the one an administration page would send, is set aside for now (owner, 2026-11-15). Its shape is not decided and it is not part of this proposal.

section.title: genro-routes#74
section.p: The options written by the recipe are not exposed to genro-org/genro-routes#74: they are written with routing.configure after the plugin is on the router, not read from the decorator. The hook must run after server.arm_router has plugged the plugins of the plugins section; before that, a block naming one of them meets a router without that plugin.

decision.question: Where does the recipe hold the plugin options of the routes?

option.title: Under each application element

list.item: The path is relative to the application.
Removing the application from the recipe removes its options.
An application added to a running server and the spawned process of an application find the options in the node they already read.
The changed rules of an installation sit in one place per application.

option.title: One section for the whole server

list.item: All the changed rules are read in one place.
Each line names the application; a line can name an application that is not there.

option.title: Both: from the server or from the application

decision.choice: Plugin configurations belong to the application only. The form starting from the server was admitted during the discussion and then withdrawn.

decision.question: What is the name of the element under application?

option.title: plugin
option.p: The server-level plugins section already has plugin children with another function: switching plugins on.

option.title: plugin_configuration

decision.question: How is a configuration written inside the application?

option.title: From the route: route(path).configure(...)
option.p: All the options changed on one route are read together. Each line must also name the plugin.

option.title: One block per plugin: plugin_configuration('auth'), then configure(path, options)
option.p: All the rules of one plugin are read in one block. The options changed on one route sit in one block per plugin.

option.title: One block per application, each line with the target "plugin/path"
option.p: A list of these lines is already a JSON form.

decision.choice: From a human point of view the plugins are configured separately.

decision.question: What does a configure line carry?

option.title: What routing.configure asks: the path and the parameters of the plugin (rule, channels)
The keywords of @route: auth_rule, channel_channels

decision.choice: kajenn calls the configure of the routing class: what the recipe holds is what that method asks.

decision.question: Which plugins can the recipe configure?

option.title: Every plugin present on the router

list.item: No list to maintain in kajenn; a plugin registered from outside is configured like the others.
The recipe can change the contract of a route: pydantic with disabled removes the validation, openapi with method changes the HTTP method the route answers.

option.title: A closed list: auth, channel, env, openapi

decision.question: What happens when the recipe names a route that does not exist?

option.title: The boot stops
At most a warning; the boot goes on

decision.question: Where does one read which options the recipe changed?

option.title: Log lines when the configuration is applied
A route of _server listing the changed options
A field in the discovery and in the OpenAPI document
Nothing added: nodes() for a user and the export of genro-routes

decision.choice: Calling nodes as a user says whether that user can or cannot. genro-routes has an export of the configuration.

decision.question: Does a second hook run after the configuration is applied?

option.title: Yes: the pair before and after gives the two exports to compare
No: a method compares the export taken before with the current state

decision.choice: Who wants the differences has a method that takes the saved export and compares it with the current state.

decision.question: Who applies the configuration, and who can refuse it or take the export before it is applied?

option.title: A plugin_configuration hook of the application, called with applications_broadcast

list.item: Words of the owner, 2026-11-15: a hook before any configuration that does not come from the code, to refuse it or to take the export; a hook plugin_configuration that does nothing when there is nothing; a broadcast of plugin configuration.
The hook that applies the recipe and the hook that can refuse or take the export are one method, redefined by the subclass.
The author of an application can refuse a change on its own routes.

option.title: A hook of the server, one for all the applications
option.p: One place takes the export of every application. The author of an application cannot refuse anything.

option.title: Both: the server hook, then the application hook

decision.choice: A hook plugin_configuration that does nothing when there is nothing: a broadcast of plugin configuration.

decision.question: How does one line give a value to several routes, for example to all the routes of the section products?

option.title: A write at router level, as genro-routes does

list.item: kajenn calls routing.configure("auth", rule="staff") on the section.
list asks for staff. insert and delete keep shop_admin, because the code gives them a rule. No message says so.

option.title: Every route under the section

list.item: kajenn calls routing.configure("auth/*", rule="staff") on the section and on every section under it.
A longer path wins, whatever the order of the lines.
A route added by a new version of the application takes the rule of the installation.

option.title: A path must end with the name of an entry; the last segment accepts the glob of the method

list.item: 'products/*' covers the three routes; 'products/insert,delete' covers two; 'products' alone gives the warning.
The glob does not descend into the sections under products.
Two lines on the same route are decided by the order of writing.

option.title: route holds several complete paths separated by commas
option.p: Every route is written by name. No glob and no path of a section.

decision.question: When does the server call the hook?

option.title: In the lifespan startup, before on_startup

list.item: No request arrives before the configuration, also for _server and in the spawned process of an application, which answer at once.
applications_broadcast is async and register_application is sync: the call cannot sit in the registration.
A section attached in on_startup or later does not exist yet: its lines give the warning and are not applied.

option.title: After on_startup, before ready

list.item: The sections attached in on_startup exist.
_server and the applications of a spawned process already answer while on_startup runs: in that interval the rule of the code is in force.

decision.choice: Before. The configurations can also change on a running server, like other things: a subscription updates the plugins when the configuration changes.

decision.question: How does the subscription update the plugins when the configuration of a running server changes?

option.title: Only the values the new configuration holds are applied

list.item: One routing.configure call per value in the new configuration.
A route the new configuration does not name keeps the value it has: the value of the code is no longer on the router.

option.title: The values of the code are restored, then the whole block is applied again

list.item: A written, changed or removed line is handled the same way.
kajenn takes the export of the router before the first configuration and keeps it for the life of the application.
The kept export is the one d-diff-method compares with the current state.

decision.choice: A change cannot take a line away. It can only say which values there are: there are no insert or delete actions, only the new configuration.

decision.question: How does a change of the plugin configuration reach the application of a spawned process?

option.title: A message of its own: the main process sends the plugin configuration over the KajennBus
It does not: the spawned process reads the new configuration when it is relaunched
Nothing specific to plugins: every change of the configuration is carried to the spawned process

decision.choice: The problem is generic. When a process is remote, any change of the configuration, not only of plugins, must be carried to the remote process, which applies it; doing so fires its own subscriptions.

decision.question: How does an application added to a running server receive the hook?

option.title: The hook is called on that application alone, before its on_startup
A new broadcast, which calls the hook again on every application

decision.question: What happens when a line names a plugin that is not on the router, or an option the plugin does not know?

option.title: The boot stops
The line is not applied and the boot goes on, as for a route that does not exist

decision.choice: Nothing happens. Whoever wrote the line wrong answers for it.

decision.question: How does a hook refuse a configuration, and what does the server do then?

option.title: The subclass does not call the base: nothing is applied and nothing is reported
The hook raises: on_error logs it and the broadcast goes on
The hook raises: the boot stops

decision.choice: As a rule, errors cannot be prevented with defensive code at every moment. If there are errors there are consequences. Only the stupid errors can be prevented; the dangerous ones pass anyway.

decision.question: At boot, who calls the hook of an application declared with spawner? The broadcast of the main process runs before on_startup, and RemoteApplication.on_startup is what waits for the spawned process to join: a hook forwarded before that has no process to answer it. The spawned process is a server too and has its own lifespan.

option.title: The spawned process, in its own lifespan startup
option.p: Default of this outline. It is settled during the implementation on a branch.

list.item: The hook runs before any request of that process, like in the main process.
RemoteApplication defines plugin_configuration itself, so the name stays local and is not forwarded, as it does for on_startup.

option.title: The main process, with the forwarded hook, once the spawned process has joined

list.item: No method to add to RemoteApplication.
The spawned process answers requests from its start: between its start and the forwarded call the values of the code are in force.

decision.question: Who provides the method that compares the saved export with the current state, and what is its name?

option.title: kajenn provides it on the application
option.p: Candidate name from the words of the owner: config_diff. kajenn then also takes and keeps the export.

option.title: Each application that wants it writes it in its own hook
option.p: Default of this outline. It is settled during the implementation on a branch.
asqueel-migration makes the same comparison of two dicts with the library dictdiffer, which is not a dependency of kajenn.

decision.question: Which keywords carry the plugin and the path in the recipe? A value written without a name is lost on a node that receives children, so the plugin of plugin_configuration needs a keyword.

option.title: plugin_configuration(code="auth") and configure(path="products/list", ...)
option.p: code is the keyword of the existing plugin element.

option.title: plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") and configure(target="products/list", ...)
option.p: target is the word of routing.configure.

option.title: plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") and configure(route="products/list", ...)

list.item: The hook depends on applications_broadcast and @broadcast_hook of kajenn-org/kajenn#142, merged in develop with PR 147.
No application can have a route named plugin_configuration: issue 142 refuses a route with the name of a @broadcast_hook.

Carrying a change of the configuration to a spawned process is a general mechanism and is not part of this proposal. It does not exist today: until it does, a change made on a running server reaches only the applications of the main process. The live configuration is the subject of kajenn-org/kajenn#75; the requirement is noted there in a comment of 2026-11-15.
A recipe can open a route its author closed. The author who must prevent it redefines the hook.
The OpenAPI document follows the recipe with no other change: security is derived from the rule in force.
The configuration guide gets a section on plugin_configuration with the Shop example.
